You were raised in the Church of the Hearth. You have recited the Gift of the Flame a thousand times. Mother Aubrine wrote to you herself, asking you to come home to Emberwick.
You ran with the river smugglers once. Rook remembers you, and remembers that you still owe the Ash Market for a job that went wrong.
You learned your trade from Lark, the last songkeeper, who taught you the Warden songs and then vanished.
You stood up for Emberwick once, and the town still tells the story. Now the town is going hungry, and they're looking at you again.
Tobin Fell taught you your craft at his ember-forge. His forge is going cold, and so is yours.
You lived alone for years on the burned bank near Old Maud, and never once used ember-fire. Your memory is the sharpest in the Vale.
Your family is minor gentry that owes everything to the Marrowbys. Lady Celandine has asked you, personally, to make sure the adventurers don't upset the town's arrangements.
You weren't born in the Vale. You came over the Greywall as a child with no memory of the crossing, and you have always dreamed of a fire.
You came to Emberwick to study the ember under the ford. You've noticed gaps in your own notes, in your own handwriting, about things you don't remember.
You worked the river boats from Emberwick's docks. You've seen what moves at night under the Ash Market's lanterns.
You served in the ford garrison under Dagna Holt. You were on the bridge the day the goblins took it, and you lived.
You grew up on Emberwick's streets with Pip, and you look out for her. Lately she's been remembering things that frighten you both.

You were raised in the Church of the Hearth. You have recited the Gift of the Flame a thousand times. Mother Aubrine wrote to you herself, asking you to come home to Emberwick.
You ran with the river smugglers once. Rook remembers you, and remembers that you still owe the Ash Market for a job that went wrong.
You learned your trade from Lark, the last songkeeper, who taught you the Warden songs and then vanished.
You stood up for Emberwick once, and the town still tells the story. Now the town is going hungry, and they're looking at you again.
Tobin Fell taught you your craft at his ember-forge. His forge is going cold, and so is yours.
You lived alone for years on the burned bank near Old Maud, and never once used ember-fire. Your memory is the sharpest in the Vale.
Your family is minor gentry that owes everything to the Marrowbys. Lady Celandine has asked you, personally, to make sure the adventurers don't upset the town's arrangements.
You weren't born in the Vale. You came over the Greywall as a child with no memory of the crossing, and you have always dreamed of a fire.
You came to Emberwick to study the ember under the ford. You've noticed gaps in your own notes, in your own handwriting, about things you don't remember.
You worked the river boats from Emberwick's docks. You've seen what moves at night under the Ash Market's lanterns.
You served in the ford garrison under Dagna Holt. You were on the bridge the day the goblins took it, and you lived.
You grew up on Emberwick's streets with Pip, and you look out for her. Lately she's been remembering things that frighten you both.
